authoritative_context_note: The fresh-checkout context is authoritative because it is reproducible from the TRACKED repository alone. The verified-environment context depends on a gitignored machine-local artifact and is disclosed, not relied upon.
registry_inventory_fingerprint_note: Derived from the loaded registry for reporting and diffing only. It does NOT define the expected control set; the registry itself does.

local_evidence_artifact.note: This artifact is gitignored and is NOT repository state. It is bound to a different commit than the current head, so the verified-environment context it produces is a MACHINE-LOCAL observation, not a repository fact.

measurement_class_legend.BEHAVIORALLY_PROVEN: A probe executed and the control's condition was met.
measurement_class_legend.BEHAVIORALLY_FAILED: A probe executed and the control's condition was NOT met.
measurement_class_legend.IMPLEMENTED_BUT_UNMEASURED: The capability demonstrably exists but no evaluator measures it, so the control defaults to BLOCKED. This is NOT a behavioural failure.
measurement_class_legend.ABSENT: The capability genuinely does not exist.
measurement_class_legend.NOT_EVALUABLE: A prerequisite (service, evidence artifact, configuration) is unavailable.
measurement_class_legend.EXTERNAL: Resolution is owned outside engineering and must never be self-approved.

curated_prose_disclosure: implemented_capability, missing_capability, estimated_effort, technical_dependencies, external_dependencies and notes are AUTHOR-SUPPLIED commentary. They are not derived from any evaluator and no guard can verify them, because there is no source of truth to check them against. The authoritative, machine-derived fields are current_disposition_fresh_checkout and blocking_reason, both produced by ga_readiness.evaluate_blockers; where the commentary and those fields disagree, the derived fields govern.

verified_environment_with_evidence.note: Measured against the local evidence artifact.

controls.resolution_condition: Audit entry hashes are computed with a managed secret key (HMAC), so a state-file writer cannot forge a valid chain.
controls.blocking_reason: Keyed audit integrity is implemented but the control is BLOCKED because no active managed HMAC key is configured (audit events are legacy/unkeyed). Configure a >=32-byte managed audit secret the state-file writer does not control.
controls.implemented_capability: Versioned HMAC-SHA256 audit chain with key rotation and retained verification-only keys; the probe signs a fresh event and requires a public-SHA forgery to be rejected. Backed by an 86-check behavioural guard. Evaluates PASS whenever an active key is set.
controls.missing_capability: No code gap. The control reads BLOCKED only when the evaluated environment has no MONDAY_REPORT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY. The resolution phrase 'a state-file writer cannot forge' additionally assumes key custody separate from the state file, which env-var injection on the same host does not by itself establish.
controls.notes: The GA client env generator previously omitted this key entirely, producing an environment in which every protected route failed closed. Fixed on this branch.

controls.resolution_condition: An externally persisted append-only anchor (event count + head hash) exists so deleting trailing events breaks integrity verification.
controls.blocking_reason: Unresolved control: Deleting the most recent N audit events leaves an internally consistent chain that still verifies as sealed; truncation is undetectable.
controls.implemented_capability: None. HMAC protects entry content, not entry existence.
controls.missing_capability: An external anchor in a second trust domain. audit_integrity_status derives total_events from len(events), so a truncated chain still verifies clean -- the project proves this deliberately in its own guard.
external_dependencies: external anchor service or immutable object-lock storage
controls.notes: docs/AUDIT_INTEGRITY.md explicitly rejects a same-process checkpoint as a substitute.

controls.implemented_capability: None. The only repository-wide match for pg_dump/RPO/RTO is the registry entry itself.
controls.missing_capability: A backup mechanism, an evidenced restore drill, and organizationally approved RPO/RTO.

controls.resolution_condition: Authenticated per-user credentials replace the single shared API key and the request actor is derived from the caller's identity.
controls.blocking_reason: Unresolved control: The whole auth surface is one shared static API key; there is no per-user identity. Required before any per-user attribution or RBAC can be trusted.
controls.implemented_capability: Per-user identity is implemented: opaque high-entropy credentials, SHA-256 + optional pepper at-rest hashing with constant-time compare, non-secret fingerprints, active/revoked credential status, per-user records with roles and account_status, admin-gated HTTP provisioning, an offline provisioning CLI, request-scoped identity in a ContextVar, and audit actor fields derived from the resolved caller. Client mode explicitly REJECTS the legacy shared key for authentication.
controls.missing_capability: No behavioural evaluator exists, so the control defaults to BLOCKED. Closing it honestly requires an evidence-driven probe plus a behavioural guard exercising real routes, and removal of the assertion that currently pins it BLOCKED.
controls.notes: The registry DESCRIPTION for this control is stale -- it predates the authenticated identity work. The RESOLUTION CONDITION is not stale and is not modified.

controls.resolution_condition: Multi-entity mutations run under a transaction/lock; no cross-process whole-snapshot last-writer-wins.
controls.blocking_reason: Persistence locking not proven: no atomicity evidence artifact.
controls.implemented_capability: Nothing for application mutations. The universal pattern is refresh() -> mutate in memory -> save() rewriting the entire payload. The local store's tmp-file + replace is atomic FILE replacement only; it prevents torn files, not lost updates. PostgresStateStore.save() is a single-statement whole-payload upsert whose preceding read uses a separate connection and therefore a separate transaction.
controls.missing_capability: No SELECT FOR UPDATE, no advisory lock, no revision/CAS column, no conflict retry, no idempotency key. The only advisory lock in the repository belongs to the migration runner, which this control explicitly excludes. Three in-process RLocks concede last-writer-wins across processes in their own comments.
controls.notes: Resolution language quoted verbatim: 'Multi-entity mutations run under a transaction/lock; no cross-process whole-snapshot last-writer-wins.' It does NOT mandate normalized tables, so a transactional snapshot with row locking and revision compare-and-swap can satisfy it.

controls.resolution_condition: A production-database-adapter-evidence.v1 artifact validates against the contract module: a named production target that is NOT a loopback or docker-bridge endpoint, NOT a test, staging or development environment and NOT ephemeral storage, with verified TLS and configured credential rotation; a non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS runtime role that does not own protected tables and is distinct from the migration administrator; full 40-character commit and tree binding to the evaluated head; a strict clean-worktree attestation re-checked at validation time; a verified canonical payload hash; production_parity=true supported by recorded observations rather than a literal; every required production proof domain accepted with domain-appropriate provenance, where recovery and availability domains require an executed drill; and a clean secret scan.
controls.blocking_reason: No valid production database-adapter evidence. A functional PostgreSQL runtime in disposable test infrastructure does not establish a production adapter: no production database-adapter evidence artifact
controls.implemented_capability: An ACCEPTED static evidence contract (production-database-adapter-evidence.v1) with a fail-closed validator and an isolated readiness consumer. A functional PostgresStateStore exists with RLS enabled and forced, proven on the accepted restricted runtime.
controls.missing_capability: No production database-adapter evidence artifact exists at any commit. The control now requires one: a named production target that is not loopback/docker-bridge, not a test/staging/development environment and not ephemeral storage, with verified TLS, credential rotation, least-privilege runtime roles, executed backup/restore and failover drills, monitoring and capacity thresholds. A disposable PostgreSQL, the restricted runtime functional matrix, tenant-authorization evidence and the dual-backend UI proof are each explicitly non-qualifying.
controls.notes: Static contract ACCEPTED; production execution NOT accepted. Contract acceptance is not adapter acceptance.

controls.resolution_condition: A production-queue-adapter-evidence.v1 artifact validates against the contract module: a named production target that is NOT a loopback or docker-bridge endpoint and NOT a test, staging or development environment, with verified TLS, configured credential rotation and an eviction policy that cannot discard a queued job; least-privilege producer and consumer identities that are neither administrative, default nor unauthenticated, an administrative identity separated from them, a per-tenant namespace binding and a rejected payload tenant override; an explicitly declared delivery model with both its loss window and its idempotency compatibility observed; full 40-character commit and tree binding to the evaluated head; a strict clean-worktree attestation re-checked at validation time; a verified canonical payload hash; production_parity=true supported by recorded observations rather than a literal; every required production queue proof domain accepted with domain-appropriate provenance, where failover, recovery, retry, poison-message and duplicate-delivery domains require an executed drill; and a clean secret scan.
controls.blocking_reason: No valid production queue-adapter evidence. A reachable queue in disposable test infrastructure does not establish a production queue adapter: no production queue-adapter evidence artifact
controls.implemented_capability: An ACCEPTED static evidence contract (production-queue-adapter-evidence.v1) with a fail-closed validator and an isolated readiness consumer. The queue itself is a best-effort index over authoritative store state.
controls.missing_capability: No production queue-adapter evidence artifact exists at any commit, and the present queue cannot satisfy the contract: delivery is at-most-once, enqueue is a non-atomic SADD+RPUSH, dequeue is an LPOP with no lease or acknowledgement, the loss window is PERMANENT because the dedupe-set entry blocks re-derivation, and there is no retry counter, dead-letter queue or per-tenant namespace in the queue keys. Queue reachability (a liveness ping), a disposable Docker Redis, the restricted worker matrix, tenant-authorization evidence, the dual-backend UI proof and production DATABASE-adapter evidence are each explicitly non-qualifying.
controls.notes: Static contract ACCEPTED; production execution NOT accepted. Contract acceptance is not adapter acceptance.
